newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - Prices up after PPI.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - Prices up after PPI.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices rose 1/4 to 3/8 of a point in early trade as U.S. producer prices' fifth straight monthly drop bolstered U.S. Treasuries.
"People are marking some bonds up 1/4 to 3/8," one municipal trader said. "I don't think they've proven any big levels yet, but they are trying to."

The Labor Department reported May PPI down 0.3 percent both overall and in the core rate, which excludes food and energy prices. The news marked the first time in 45 years that wholesale prices declined for five consecutive months.

In the goverment market, the benchmark 30-year bond was up 14/32 at 98-16/32 to yield 6.74 percent. In debt futures, the September municipal contract was up 4/32 at 117-20/32. The September T-bond contract was up 9/32 at 111-21/32. The MOB spread was 191 ticks.

Friday's actively quoted issues included Dade County, Fla., 5-1/4 percent water and sewer system revenue bonds of October 2026. The bonds had a 5.49 percent net bid, versus a 5.51 percent net bid on Thursday.
Thursday's session, which closed up roughly 1/2 point, saw a fair amount of institional selling, traders said. One trader said 12 to 15 institutions had lists out.
"I thought a lot of people wanted to sell into it, and they put big prices on stuff hoping they'd get it," he said. "I think they are going to do a little bit of that today, although not as much."
In new issues, Robinson-Humphrey Co tentatively priced $48 million Spartanburg County, S.C., Health Services District hospital revenue refunding bonds at a top yield of 5.58 percent in 2022.
